item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 apps: Introducing Update Repair in Inventory
item.description:
[What and why]

We are introducing Update Repair in Inventory to help admins identify and remediate Windows devices with Microsoft 365 apps that are out of date or experiencing update issues. In the Microsoft 365 apps admin center, admins can review device status and recommended actions, remotely start Online Repair for eligible devices, and follow manual remediation guidance for devices that need attention. Repair reinstalls Microsoft 365 apps using the latest available build for the device's configured update channel.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Rollout began in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 and is expected to complete by late November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Admins managing Windows devices with Microsoft 365 apps installed.

Platforms and services

  • Windows devices with Microsoft 365 apps
  • Microsoft 365 apps admin center

What will happen

  • Admins can more easily identify devices with Microsoft 365 apps update issues and decide how to remediate them.
  • Eligible devices can be repaired remotely, reducing the need for hands-on intervention.
  • Repair closes open Office apps and reinstalls Microsoft 365 apps.
  • Devices that need attention still require administrator review and manual remediation.

[Action required and recommendations]

  • Go to the Microsoft 365 apps admin center and make sure Inventory is enabled.
  • Update Repair uses Inventory data from Windows devices with Microsoft 365 apps installed to identify devices that need attention or repair. For the Repair action, devices must be running build 16.0.20326.20000 or later.
  • Before starting a repair, notify affected users, ask them to save their work and close Office apps, and schedule the action to minimize disruption.
  • Keep devices powered on, signed in, and connected so they can receive the action at their next Inventory check-in.

[Learn more]

  • Use Update Repair to identify and remediate Microsoft 365 Apps update issues - Microsoft 365 Apps | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Updated Photos experience on Windows 11
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We're introducing an updated Photos experience on Windows 11 to help people browse, organize, and find photos and videos across their PC and OneDrive. The experience is coming to consumer and commercial devices and will continue to respect existing controls for app installation, updates, and OneDrive access.

Starting October 15, 2026, the updated experience is expected to roll out to Windows Insiders over the next few days. We expect to start expanding to Windows 11 Retail users on October 26.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 568931

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on mid October 2026 and expect to complete by mid December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users will continue to find Photos in Start. The updated experience includes a refreshed photo library, a native Photo Viewer for images opened from File Explorer or elsewhere in Windows, and an updated native photo editor. People can use Photos with local content without signing in to OneDrive. Users who sign in with a work or school account can see their OneDrive photos alongside local content.

Existing management controls continue to apply:

  • If your organization disables or removes Store-originated apps using DisableStoreApps, the update will not be installed on affected devices.
  • If you use AppLocker packaged-app rules to block Microsoft Photos, update those rules to include the package Microsoft.OneDrive.Photos if you intend to keep blocking it.
  • DisablePersonalSync prevents personal OneDrive account sign-in in Photos. DisableNucleusSync prevents the use of any OneDrive account in Photos. These policies restrict OneDrive functionality in Photos; they do not prevent people from using the app with local content.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

For most organizations, no new or immediate configuration is required. Review your existing Windows app-management and OneDrive policies, especially rules that intentionally block or remove Photos. If you use AppLocker to block Photos, account for the updated package name. Share this change with your help desk if users may have questions about the updated experience.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft OneDrive: OneDrive sync supports up to 1 million items on macOS
item.description:
[What and why]

In MC1294528, we announced an increase to the item sync limit for OneDrive on Windows. We are now increasing the same item sync limit for OneDrive on macOS: from 300,000 items to 1 million items per sync instance, per device. This increase is designed to help organizations with large OneDrive and SharePoint libraries sync more content reliably across devices.

The capability will be available first in Public Preview for devices enrolled in the Insiders ring, and later in General Availability. Devices that do not meet the minimum hardware and configuration requirements will continue to sync at the existing supported limit of 300,000 items without disruption.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users syncing OneDrive, OneDrive for Business, or SharePoint document libraries on macOS.
  • Users with libraries that approach or exceed the current supported sync limit of 300,000 items.
  • Preview participants using the Insiders ring.

Platforms and services

  • macOS
  • OneDrive
  • OneDrive for Business
  • SharePoint document libraries

What will happen

  • macOS devices that meet the minimum hardware and configuration requirements can sync up to 1 million items per sync instance. Devices that do not meet these requirements will see no change in behavior.
  • No disruption to existing sync configurations is expected.

Note: Performance is not yet optimized for syncing a high volume of read-only files or for accounts under legal hold. We are actively working to improve performance and reliability for these scenarios.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required if you do not plan to participate in Public Preview. If you plan to evaluate this capability:

  • Identify users and devices with large OneDrive or SharePoint libraries that may benefit from the increased sync limit.
  • Ensure devices meet the minimum hardware and configuration requirements (i.e., supported operating system, memory, storage, and processor).
  • Review the recommended sync configuration for OneDrive and SharePoint sync reliability.
  • Inform helpdesk staff and affected users that Public Preview requires the Insiders ring and that devices that do not meet the minimum hardware and configuration requirements will remain at the current supported limit.

[Learn more]

  • Recommended sync app configuration - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
  • Restrictions and limitations in OneDrive and SharePoint | Microsoft Support
  • The OneDrive sync app update process - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Migrate Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing before EWS deprecation
item.description:
Updated October 20, 2026: Gov rollout of this feature is paused at this time. We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for any inconvenience.

[What and Why:]

Exchange Web Services (EWS) deprecation begins October 1, 2026. Cross-tenant collaboration features — Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing — currently rely on EWS.

Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips will be available by September 2026 and Calendar Sharing will be available by end-October 2026 via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy, which replaces EWS-based cross-tenant collaboration.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in August 2026 and expect to complete by September 15, 2026 for Free/Busy, Mailtips and October 30, 2026 for Calendar Sharing.
  • GCC, GCC High, DoD: We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[Impact on your organization:]

Sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips (e.g., out of office message) with another Microsoft 365 organization via Organization Relationship or Sharing Policy relies on Exchange Web Services (EWS), which is being deprecated. To preserve these cross-tenant collaboration scenarios, you will need to start migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policy.

Your tenant is affected if it uses any of the following Exchange Online configurations:

  • Organization Relationships — sharing Free/Busy or MailTips with other Microsoft 365 tenants 
  • Sharing Policies — sharing calendars externally, either via invitations sent to recipients in other Microsoft 365 organizations or calendars published for anonymous access via an internet URL

Run these commands in Exchange Online PowerShell to check if your tenant is affected: 

    • Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScopeIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) either FreeBusyAccessEnabled: True or MailtipsAccessEnabled: True, and (3) the external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed. 
    • Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Domains, Enabled, DefaultIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) the Domains property contains at least one rule with a CalendarSharingFreeBusy access level (Simple, Detail, or Reviewer), and (3) the targeted external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, and (4) the policy is assigned to one or more mailboxes, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed.
    • Note: rules that begin with Anonymous: represent calendar publishing to anonymous internet recipients via a published URL - these also appear in this output.

What happens if I do nothing:

Starting October 1, 2026, Exchange Web Services (EWS) will be gradually disabled in line with previous communications linked to this message. As this rollout reaches your tenant, cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing that rely on EWS will be affected — recipients in partner organizations may no longer see Free/Busy, MailTips, or shared calendars from your tenant. 

If your organization is not ready to migrate, you can retain EWS access by following the guidance of the latest blog we published: ExchangeOnline EWS, Your Time is Almost Up (EWSEnabled set to True) while you prepare and execute the migration steps attached to this message. EWS access through this extension will remain available until the final EWS shutdown on April 1, 2027. 

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Follow this Message center post for updates to the rollout schedule. To avoid impact, plan to migrate after the rollout reaches your tenant and before EWS deprecation.
  • Review the migration guide linked below for step-by-step instructions to understand your current configurations, set up new Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policies, validate the new configurations, and remove unused configurations. 
  • Check the blog post linked below for additional information and answers to frequently asked questions. 
  • Hybrid and on-premises scenarios are not in scope. This update applies to fully cloud-hosted (Exchange Online ↔ Exchange Online) cross-tenant and cross-cloud configurations only. For organizations running on-premises Exchange and Exchange Online in a Hybrid Deployment, migrate to Dedicated Hybrid App. For organizations hosted in Exchange Online sharing with another organization running Exchange on-premises, kindly monitor future Message Center posts for guidance on migration paths as they become available. 

[Additional information:]

  • Migration guide: Migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy for sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips.
  • Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy Microsoft Graph API Overview
  • Exchange Online EWS, Your Time is Almost Up
  • Deprecation of EWS in Exchange Online 
  • Enhancing Microsoft 365 security by eliminating high-privilege access 
  • Blog Post: Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing are moving to Cross-Tenant Access Policy

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Review PDFs using the Copilot context menu on OneDrive iOS
item.description:
Updated October 20, 2026: We have decided not to move forward with this change at this time. We apologize for any inconvenience. 

[What and why:]

Microsoft 365 Copilot makes PDF reviews faster and easier on mobile. Select text in any PDF in OneDrive iOS and tap Ask Copilot to explain, summarize, translate, or ask a custom question about the selection — the same in-context Copilot experience already generally available on desktop, now on OneDrive iOS.

[When this will happen:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We have decided not to move forward with this change at this time. 

[Impact on your organization:]

When this rolls out, users viewing a PDF in OneDrive iOS can select text and see Ask Copilot in the context menu. Tapping it opens Copilot with the selected text as context, so they can:

  • Explain dense or technical passages in plain language
  • Summarize long sections
  • Translate into another language
  • Custom prompt: add their own prompt for tailored results — no need to switch apps

The feature is on by default where Copilot is enabled.

Steps to use Ask Copilot in OneDrive iOS:

  1. Open the OneDrive app on iOS and sign in with your work account.
  2. Open the PDF you want to review.
  3. Select any text in the PDF. The context menu will display Ask Copilot.
  4. Tap Ask Copilot for a plain-language explanation or type your own prompt for tailored results.

Licensing requirements

A Microsoft 365 Copilot license is required to use this feature.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

No admin action is required. You may want to:

  • Review your Copilot license assignments for mobile users.
  • Update user-facing training/help content to mention Ask Copilot in PDFs on OneDrive iOS.
  • Notify your help desk of the new entry point.

Note: Some users may see this feature before others in your organization.

[Compliance considerations:]

This feature follows your existing Copilot data-handling and enterprise data protection commitments. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center - Let representatives set next presence to handle routing of work items
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to allow representatives to set next presence to indicate their future availability in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. This feature will reach general availability on October 30, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Next presence allows service representatives to queue their next availability status and stop receiving new assignments while the next presence status is pending. After all active conversations and work items are completed, the system automatically updates the representative's presence to the selected status. This setting allows representatives to transition smoothly to breaks or other availability states without interrupting customer engagements or requiring manual status changes.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Enable and update next presence.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Purview | Data Lifecycle Management - Graph API Support for archive mailboxes
item.description:
[What and why]

As part of the retirement of Exchange Web Services (EWS) in Exchange Online, Microsoft is expanding support for archive mailbox scenarios through Microsoft Graph APIs.

Organizations that currently use EWS to access archive mailbox data should begin migrating to Microsoft Graph APIs before EWS is disabled. Microsoft Graph now provides API support for importing and exporting mailbox data and for managing archive mailbox folders, including support for auto-expanding archives.

This change helps ensure continued access to archive mailbox data after EWS is retired and provides a supported path forward for compliance, data lifecycle management, eDiscovery, backup, and related archive mailbox solutions.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by early November 2026
  • Important: Exchange Web Services (EWS) in Exchange Online will begin to be disabled globally in October 2026 and is expected to be fully disabled by April 2027

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

Organizations that use applications, scripts, or third-party solutions that rely on EWS to access archive mailbox content.

Examples include:

  • eDiscovery solutions
  • Compliance and records management workflows
  • Data lifecycle management solutions
  • Backup and export tools
  • Custom applications that access archive mailboxes

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview
  • Exchange Online
  • Microsoft Graph

What will happen

  • Applications and scripts that continue to use EWS for archive mailbox operations will stop functioning after EWS is disabled.
  • Organizations using auto-expanding archive mailboxes must update applications to support Microsoft Graph archive mailbox behaviors.
  • Microsoft Graph APIs support archive mailbox scenarios through:
    • Mailbox import and export APIs
    • MailboxFolder APIs for folder management operations
  • Applications may need to handle redirect responses when archive content resides in auxiliary archive mailboxes.

[Action required and recommendations]

Action required: Yes

Before October 2026, we recommend that administrators and developers:

  • Identify applications and scripts that use EWS to access archive mailboxes.
    • Review EWS Usage Reports: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/activity-reports/ews-usage
  • Review Microsoft Graph archive mailbox guidance.
    • Review Archive mailbox redirects: https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/handle-archive-mailbox-redirects
  • Update applications to use Microsoft Graph APIs for archive mailbox operations.
    • Review Mailbox import and export overview: https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/mailbox-import-export-concept-overview
  • Use available migration resources to assess and update existing code.
    • EWS Analyzer and migration tools: https://aka.ms/ewsTools
    • AI-assisted migration tutorial: https://aka.ms/ewsToolsAITutorial
    • EWS-to-Microsoft Graph API mappings: https://aka.ms/ews2graphMap
  • Contact third-party vendors to confirm their plans and timelines for migrating from EWS to Microsoft Graph.

Learn more

  • Deprecation of EWS in Exchange Online
  • EWS migration tools
  • Exchange Web Services (EWS) to Microsoft Graph API mappings
  • Handle archive mailbox redirects in Microsoft Graph
  • Overview of the mailbox import and export APIs in Microsoft Graph https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/mailbox-import-export-concept-overview
  • Tutorial - Migrating from EWS to Microsoft Graph API with GitHub Copilot

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change modify, interrupt, or disable Purview-related capabilities, including retention, eDiscovery, export, or data lifecycle management workflows?Yes. Organizations using EWS-based integrations for eDiscovery, compliance exports, retention-related processes, or data lifecycle management that access archive mailboxes must migrate to Microsoft Graph APIs before EWS is disabled.
Does this change alter how users or applications access, export, or manage Microsoft 365 data?Yes. Applications that access or export archive mailbox data through EWS must be updated to use Microsoft Graph APIs to maintain functionality after EWS retirement.
Does this change add or affect third-party integrations?Yes. Third-party applications and services that use EWS to access archive mailbox content may require vendor-provided updates or migration to Microsoft Graph APIs.
Does this change affect how organizations demonstrate or maintain compliance processes?Yes. Organizations that rely on EWS-based compliance, auditing, export, or records management workflows for archive mailbox data should review and update their integrations to ensure continuity of compliance operations.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] (Updated) Windows updates are available for 2026 time zone changes in Canada
item.description:
(Updated October 16, 2026: Added guidance for managing the Alberta and British Columbia time zone changes in Outlook Time Zone Changes for Alberta and British Columbia.)

What and why

Windows updates are now available to support the 2026 time zone changes in Manitoba, Alberta, and British Columbia. On November 1, 2026, clocks in affected regions will not be set back by one hour.

Manitoba will permanently stay on UTC-5, Alberta and affected locations will permanently stay on UTC-6, and most of British Columbia will permanently stay on UTC-7. The new Windows updates add region-specific time zones to support these changes.

Rollout schedule

  • September 22, 2026: The Alberta and British Columbia changes became available in the September 2026 non-security preview update for Windows 11, versions 25H2 and 24H2.
  • October 13, 2026: The Manitoba change became available for all supported versions of Windows. The Alberta and British Columbia changes became available for all other supported versions of Windows, including Windows Server. These changes are included in the October 2026 security update.
  • November 1, 2026: The time zone transitions take effect at 2:00 a.m. local time. Clocks in affected areas will not be set back by one hour.

Impact on your organization

Devices in affected regions will display an incorrect local time after the November 1, 2026 transition if the applicable Windows update is not installed or the appropriate time zone is not selected. The updates add the following region-specific time zones:

  • (UTC-05:00) Manitoba

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot for Teams: Bilingual consecutive interpretation mode with Interpreter agent
item.description:
Updated July 13, 2026: We have paused rollout of this feature at this time. We will provide an update via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for any inconvenience. 

[Introduction]

Consecutive Interpretation is a new interpretation mode available as an add‑on to the existing Interpreter agent in Microsoft Teams. It enables structured multilingual conversations in meetings by providing shared, meeting‑level interpretation when enabled by a Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed user.

This mode uses consecutive (turn‑by‑turn) interpretation, meaning participants speak one at a time and each speaker's words are interpreted before the next speaker begins. This structured flow reduces overlap, improves interpretation accuracy, and helps everyone stay aligned in real time.

Consecutive Interpretation is ideal for back‑and‑forth, interactive discussions where participants need to respond, clarify, and build on each other’s input across languages, such as working sessions, negotiations, and cross‑functional collaboration.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 557180.

[When this will happen]

  • Targeted Release: Rollout begins in early May 2026 (previously early April) and is expected to complete by late May 2026 (previously mid-April).
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will provide an update via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[How this will affect your organization]

Who is affected

  • All Microsoft 365 tenants using Microsoft Teams meetings where users are licensed with Microsoft 365 Copilot.

What will happen

  • For tenants
    • The new Consecutive Interpretation mode extends the existing Interpreter agent to support structured, interactive multilingual meetings.
    • The existing Interpreter experience remains unchanged unless this new mode is enabled.
  • For admins
    • No new tenant‑level configuration is required.
    • The feature is available to all users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
    • Existing compliance, privacy, and data‑handling policies for Interpreter continue to apply.
  • For users
    • When a Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed user enables the mode, interpretation becomes a shared meeting‑level experience rather than an individual setting.
    • Participants speak consecutively, with each turn interpreted and delivered before the next participant begins.

[What you need to do to prepare]

  • No action is required to maintain current behavior.
  • Ensure any users who intend to use this mode have an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: Upcoming change to voicemail message delivery by email

We’re changing how Microsoft Teams voicemail messages are delivered by email to improve security and give organizations more control over sender identity. Organizations will be able to send voicemail notifications from their own domain and apply existing SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and domain-protection policies to help prevent spoofing and impersonation.

Supporting organization-owned sending domains requires a new voicemail email delivery solution. Caller information will move from the email From field to the Subject line and remain in the message body.

Platforms and services

  • Voicemail

item.title: [planForChange] Upcoming changes to Agents in SharePoint and OneDrive
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We are upgrading the agent experience in SharePoint and OneDrive to better align with the Microsoft Copilot extensibility ecosystem, specifically to ensure that these agents are part of Copilot app home experiences (MC1479277) and the Microsoft plugin registry (MC1484008), the shared catalog for discovering, publishing, and governing organization-approved and custom-built plugins across Microsoft Copilot experiences (Chat, Cowork, Code, Autopilot) and Microsoft 365 apps (Word, PowerPoint, Excel), OneDrive and SharePoint.

  3. Upgrade to a declarative agent or update your custom engine agent that was published to the SharePoint channel, when users need a content-grounded, conversational experience across Microsoft 365.

  • Creating agents will use the Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder
  • An Upgrade button will appear in the SharePoint builder so you can upgrade the agent to use the Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder. 
  • A convert-agent-file-to-skill skill will be available in Copilot in SharePoint

Changes to the user experience of the site will support this transition:

  • The Agent Chat web part is coming soon to allow any agent from the Plugin store to appear on the SharePoint site with more intention and control for greater reach and impact
  • Copilot in SharePoint is already available worldwide and is coming soon to Government clouds.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide and Government clouds): This change consists of two rollouts:

  • Agent creation and upgrade: Rollout begins mid-November and is expected to complete by early December 2026
  • Agents in SharePoint and OneDrive using .agent file format stop working in SharePoint, Teams and Copilot app: Rollout begins early April and is expected to complete mid-April 2027

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Organizations using agents in SharePoint and OneDrive.
  • SharePoint site owners and members who create or manage agents in the .agent file format.
  • Admins responsible for agent governance, adoption, licensing, and support.

Platforms/Services:

  • SharePoint
  • OneDrive

  • Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder
  • Microsoft Plugin store

  • An Upgrade button appears in the SharePoint builder.
  • A convert-agent-file-to-skill skill is available in Copilot in SharePoint
  • Upgraded agents must be re-added to Teams Chat/Channel
  • With Agent Chat web part, site owners/page authors can add any agent from the Plugin store into SharePoint.

After March 2027, agents using .agent file format will stop working in SharePoint, Teams and Copilot app; including Agent Link web part, immersive experience, chat pane in SharePoint.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Begin preparing for the transition away from SharePoint and OneDrive .agent files now. Identify the teams that own or manage agents, share the March 2027 deadline, and ensure that site and agent owners understand the upgrade paths. Administrators should become familiar with Copilot in SharePoint, Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder, Agent 365 and the governance and management capabilities that will apply to upgraded experiences. 

You don’t need to change any .agent file format agents today, but the following changes will help you transition:

  1. “Create an agent”/“New agent” in SharePoint/OneDrive open Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder for creation. These agents are added to the Plugin store and will not create .agent files. 
  2. You can continue to edit existing .agent files during the transition period. When you are ready to upgrade, use the Upgrade to M365 Agent button in the SharePoint agent builder or convert-agent-file-to-skill skill in Copilot in SharePoint. 
  3. Use the Agent Chat web part to add the agent to a SharePoint page.

Review the guidance on finding and upgrading existing agents.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Simplifying AI access: Introducing usage-based billing
item.description:
Updated October 16, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

The new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business combines everyday AI via user subscription license with Advanced AI via usage-based billing. Beginning in mid-November, usage-based billing will be included by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases for tenants that have Microsoft 365 Business Premium. For CSP customers, usage-based billing will be included by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases starting December 1, 2026. This phased approach makes it easier to access eligible usage-based AI experiences, including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities, while reducing billing complexity and preserving flexibility to expand usage over time based on business needs.

You have been identified as a customer who may be affected by this phased rollout.

What is changing

  • With eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases: Beginning in mid-November, pay-as-you-go usage-based billing will be configured by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases for tenants that have Microsoft 365 Business Premium. Tenants without Microsoft 365 Business Premium will follow at a later date. 
    • For CSP customers, beginning December 1 pay-as-you-go usage-based billing will be configured by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases.
  • If your organization does not already have the required pay-as-you-go Azure resources and/or spending policy, it will be created as part of the eligible purchase and product setup. 
  • The resulting spending policy will have a spending limit of 4,000 Copilot credits per user per month with charges based on actual usage.
  • Charges apply only when these experiences are used, subject to the usage controls and spending limits established by your administrator.
  • We will begin rolling out this change to eligible customers in supported markets. The change will not initially be available in Australia, Belgium, Brazil, France, Germany, India, Italy, Korea, Netherlands, Poland, Spain. We will provide additional information about availability in these markets when available. 

What is not changing

  • Your existing Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscription benefits and payment terms do not change.
  • Capabilities already included with your license remain included; this change adds a spending policy for eligible usage-based experiences.
  • If your organization already has a spending policy configured, the existing spending policy remains in place.

When this will happen

  • Mid-November 2026: Usage-based billing default-on will begin for eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made directly from Microsoft, including through Microsoft web and the Microsoft 365 admin center, for tenants that have Microsoft 365 Copilot Business Premium.
  • Future rollout: Tenants that do not have Microsoft 365 Business Premium, including tenants that only have Microsoft 365 Business Standard and/or Basic with Copilot, or only Microsoft 365 Copilot Business.
  • Starting December 1, 2026: The change applies to eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made through Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) channels.

How usage-based billing works

  • If your organization does not already have the required pay-as-you-go Azure resource and/or spending policy, it will be created as part of the eligible purchase and product setup.
  • Administrators can review and manage usage controls and spending policy in Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Your organization can adjust its spending policies and controls to align with its needs. Disabling usage-based billing prevents access to experiences that require it.

What you can do to prepare

  • Review which eligible usage-based experiences—including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities—may support your organization’s needs.
  • Review your organization’s usage-based billing, governance, and cost-management requirements.
  • On or after the applicable date, confirm or adjust usage controls and spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 

Learn more

item.title: [planForChange] Support for Office LTSC 2021 and additional apps ended on October 13, 2026
item.description:

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Edge: Browser-native XSLT will be disabled by default
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft Edge is deprecating browser-native Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations (XSLT). Edge will disable the XSLTProcessor JavaScript API and XML processing instructions that reference XSLT stylesheets by default. XML processing instructions that reference CSS stylesheets are not affected.

The native XSLT implementation depends on an aging native codebase that processes untrusted XML and XSLT content. Removing this functionality reduces the browser attack surface. XSLT also has low modern web usage, and safer migration alternatives are available.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Organizations may be affected if internal websites, public websites, embedded-device interfaces, or third-party web applications depend on browser-native XSLT. In Microsoft Edge 159, browser-native XSLT will be off by default in Stable. The temporary XSLTEnabled policy is planned for removal in Microsoft Edge 176 in Summer 2027.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Before Microsoft Edge Stable 159, identify applications that use the XSLTProcessor JavaScript API or XML processing instructions that reference XSL stylesheets. To check for browser-native XSLT usage with Lighthouse in Microsoft Edge:

  1. Open the application in a current version of Microsoft Edge.
  2. Sign in and navigate to the application page you want to test.
  3. Open Edge DevTools with F12 or Ctrl+Shift+I.
  4. Select the Lighthouse tool. If it isn't visible, select More tools (+) > Lighthouse.
  5. Select:
    • Mode: Navigation
    • Category: Best Practices
  6. For authenticated applications: In Lighthouse Settings, turn off Clear storage so the audit preserves your signed-in session. Leave it enabled for public pages that don't require stored application state.
  7. Select Analyze page load.
  8. In the report:
    • Search for XSLT, deprecated, or XSLTProcessor.
    • Check for Uses deprecated APIs.
    • Expand Issues were logged in the DevTools Issues panel.
  9. Check the DevTools Issues and Console tools for XSLT deprecation warnings.
  10. Repeat the audit for each relevant page and exercise important application workflows.

Migrate affected applications to supported alternatives or contact the developers/vendor responsible for the affected site to update the application and remove its dependency on browser-native XSLT. If more time is needed, configure the temporary XSLTEnabled policy while application owners complete migration.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins can temporarily use the XSLTEnabled policy to manage XSLT behavior while migrating affected applications.
Does the change modify or disable a capability?Yes. Browser-native XSLT will be disabled by default and the temporary policy is planned for removal in a future Edge release.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams Rooms: Identify in-room participants with IntelliFrame people labels
item.description:

[What and Why:]

We're introducing IntelliFrame people labels in Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows to improve meeting clarity and inclusivity for remote participants. When enabled, this feature identifies in-room participants by name and displays a contact card, helping remote attendees easily recognize speakers and follow conversations.

This enhancement supports better hybrid meeting experiences by connecting in-room and remote participants more effectively, improving collaboration and productivity.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 566700.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning late January 2027 (previously mid-November 2026) expected to complete by early February 2027 (previously mid-December 2026)

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows with Teams Rooms Pro licenses
  • In-room participants who have enrolled in voice and face recognition (People Recognition)

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Teams Rooms on Windows devices
  • Supported intelligent camera hardware

What will happen:

  • IntelliFrame will display name labels under identified in-room participants’ video feeds.
  • Remote participants can select a label to view a contact card with organizational details.
  • The feature is enabled automatically when prerequisites are met.
  • Existing Teams meeting policies for voice and face enrollment are honored.
  • Participants without enrolled profiles will appear without labels.
  • No change occurs if voice and face enrollment is disabled in your organization.

Screenshot - IntelliFrame people labels identify enrolled in-room participants by name, helping remote attendees recognize who's speaking; selecting a label opens the person's contact card

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required to enable this feature.

To maximize value, administrators may:

  • Review and confirm Teams Rooms devices:
    • Ensure devices are licensed with Teams Rooms Pro.
    • Verify use of supported intelligent cameras.
  • Review and update meeting policies:
    • Allow enrollment: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -EnrollUserOverride Enabled.
    • Enable name display in rooms: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -RoomPeopleNameUserOverride On.
  • Encourage users to enroll in voice and face recognition: Teams > Settings > Recognition.
  • Update internal documentation and helpdesk guidance.
  • Notify users about this capability to drive awareness and adoption.

To disable IntelliFrame people labels, administrators can:

  • Turn off in-room name display (labels stop; other IntelliFrame framing unaffected): Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -RoomPeopleNameUserOverride Off
  • Block voice and face enrollment entirely (no one can be identified by name): Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -EnrollUserOverride Disabled
  • Individual users can opt out anytime by removing their profile in Teams > Settings > Recognition.
